sources.finding: Producing-mine recoverable reserves are working inventory, distinct from larger estimated recoverable reserves across the resource base.
Tables 11 and 14 distinguish productive capacity and recoverable reserves at producing mines; table 31 is mine sales price by rank.
U.S. coal import/export tables use origin/destination countries, not subject-country whole trade totals.
Productive capacity is potential output with existing equipment, sufficient inputs and demand; not actual production or reserves.

p.14: fuel receipt/cost reporting is limited to selected plants, including 50 MW coal-primary capacity and 200 MW specified gas/petroleum-primary capacity. Generation facility-size amendment does not extend to receipt prices.

expectationsBeforeClassifierEdit: Only all ranks and all mine types can yield whole coal production; individual ranks/types remain subsets.
Producing-mine reserves and producer/distributor stocks remain subsets even with total mine type.
Total productive mine capacity is a separate labelled whole-product capacity basis, not output.
Mine count, employees, hours, productivity and coal quality measures are outside locked activities.
Shipments/receipts are not consumption or production; shipments route is further restricted to electric-power deliveries and mine/destination place role.
Coal coke, steam and metallurgical trade are subsets of coal.
Whole U.S. trade requires both total foreign partners and total customs districts; never reinterpret partners as requested subject countries.
Import/export unit prices must carry trade-price basis, never domestic retail wording.
Other industrial and coke plants separately are not the whole industrial sector; utility/IPP breakdowns are not the whole electric-power sector.
No definition combination proves published observations.
